explain: Homebrew is one command, brew, with subcommands for each job. After it, the usual terminal shape: flags and arguments.
remember: brew + what to do + to what.

syntax:
brew install git
brew install --cask visual-studio-code
explain: A formula is a command-line tool; a cask (--cask) is an app with a window.
remember: Cask = a case for an app.

syntax:
brew update
brew upgrade
brew list
explain: update refreshes the list of what exists; upgrade installs newer versions of what you have; list shows what you have.
remember: update the menu, then upgrade the food.

explain: Subcommand (info) + flag (--cask) + argument (firefox). The same pattern as every other brew line.
Installs a command-line tool, like python or git.
Installs a desktop app, like visual-studio-code or google-chrome.
Updates Homebrew's list of available software.
Upgrades all your installed packages, or just one.
example: Getting the newest version of node.

explain: Shows everything you have installed.
example: Checking whether python is already installed.

explain: Removes a package.
example: Removing a tool you no longer use.

explain: search finds available software. info shows version details and dependencies.
example: brew info node before installing it.

explain: doctor diagnoses problems and broken links. cleanup deletes old downloads to free up space.
example: When an install fails, run brew doctor first.

syntax:
brew services start <name>
brew services stop <name>
explain: Runs a background tool (like a database) automatically on your Mac, or stops it.
Install several packages in one command.
Install a specific version with @version.
example: A project that needs an older Node.

explain: Removes and installs a package again.
Casks are apps with windows. They go into /Applications.
example: Installing your apps from the terminal.

explain: Downloads a package without installing it.
example: Getting things ready before going offline.

explain: Lists installed packages that have newer versions.
Upgrade one package, or all your casks.

syntax:
brew pin node
brew unpin node
explain: pin stops a package from being upgraded. unpin allows it again.
example: Keeping the version your project needs.

explain: List only apps, or list packages with their versions.
Shows packages you installed yourself (not ones pulled in by others).
example: Cleaning up things you no longer use.

explain: Uninstall an app. autoremove deletes packages nothing needs any more.

syntax:
brew deps node
brew uses --installed openssl
explain: deps: what a package needs. uses: what needs a package.
Search only apps.
example: Finding the exact name to install.

syntax:
brew info --cask visual-studio-code
brew desc git
explain: info shows details for an app; desc gives a one-line description.
Opens the package's website.
-n shows what would be deleted without deleting. --prune=all removes all old downloads.
Checks if any package is missing something it needs.
Shows your Homebrew setup and version.
example: Information to include when asking for help.

explain: Where Homebrew lives, where one package lives, and where downloads are kept.
Lists background services and whether they're running.
example: Checking if your database is running.

syntax:
brew services stop postgresql
brew services restart postgresql
explain: Stop or restart a background service.
example: Restarting a database after changing settings.

explain: Runs a service now, but does not start it at login.

syntax:
brew link node@20 --force
brew unlink node
explain: link makes a version the one the terminal uses; unlink removes it.

syntax:
brew tap
brew tap homebrew/cask-fonts
brew untap homebrew/cask-fonts
explain: A tap is an extra list of packages. tap with no name lists the ones you have.
example: Getting packages that aren't in the main list.

explain: dump writes everything you installed into a Brewfile. bundle installs everything in it.
example: Setting up a new Mac exactly like your old one.

explain: A Brewfile: one line per package. Keep it in your dotfiles.
The official command to install Homebrew itself (from brew.sh).
Adds Homebrew to your PATH. Put it in ~/.zprofile on Apple Silicon Macs.

syntax:
brew help
brew commands
brew help install
explain: Lists commands and explains one.
Stops Homebrew from sending anonymous usage data.
Shows the history of changes to a package's formula.
example: Seeing what changed in an update.

explain: Resets Homebrew's own files when brew update keeps failing.

syntax: brew install wget tree jq htop
explain: wget downloads, tree shows folders as a tree, jq reads JSON, htop shows running programs.

syntax:
brew install gh
gh auth login
explain: gh is GitHub's command-line tool.
example: Making pull requests from the terminal.

explain: Rectangle snaps windows, iTerm2 is a popular terminal app.
example: Making your Mac nicer to code on.

syntax:
brew install postgresql@16
brew services start postgresql@16
explain: Install a database and start it in the background.
example: Local database for a web app.
